name: THORSwap TSAggregatorGeneric swapIn makes an arbitrary call that spends approvals to the aggregator
summary: TSAggregatorGeneric.swapIn(router, vault, memo, token, amount, swapRouter, data, deadline) pulls amount of token from the caller through its token transfer proxy and then calls swapRouter with caller-supplied data, refusing only the proxy itself as target. Wallets that had approved the aggregator directly could therefore be drained by calling swapIn with WBNB, amount 0, swapRouter set to a token and data transferFrom(wallet, attacker, balance). The anchor's contract made nine such swapIn calls, taking DAI, ADA, USDC, USDT, LTC and ETH from nine approvers.

campaign.selection: transactions after 0x077ea419 in which the aggregator 0xb6fa6f1d spent a wallet's allowance to itself (an Approval with spender 0xb6fa6f1d emitted by transferFrom) in a transaction not sent by that wallet; 599.999 USDC and 1,287.86 USDT taken from 0xadbdb8d5, 0x5c9798f0, 0xca987722, 0x0f67e1b3 and 0xf3426661

notes: Anchor is 0x0000000000004f3d's transaction via its contract 0x000000000000e59f, four days before the DeFiHackLabs transaction 0x077ea419 (Defimon alert 1277, 1,300 USDT from 0x806ac20b, which had also lost 86 USDT in the anchor). Nothing went back to the wallets; the DAI moved on to 0xdfac7733 and 0x44487a44.

Earlier exploits were searched through every Approval with spender 0xb6fa6f1d on BSC from the aggregator's deployment to the chain head: 15 wallets approved it directly on 2025-05-28 (blocks 50457615-50461986) and the anchor is the first transaction that spent such an allowance without being sent by its owner (the BEP-20 tokens involved emit Approval on transferFrom). campaign.mjs cannot finish here (over 10,000 swapIn calls), so this event scan stands in for it; it also yields the DeFiHackLabs transaction and the 46-transaction bundle, which runs to 2026-10-20 because the aggregator was never changed.

Direct, immutable deployment; the only later state change before the anchor is setFee(0) at block 50161393, a fee value that does not reset the age (rule 8). None of the same deployer's 87 other contracts on BSC, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Avalanche and Base has this bytecode, and no THORSwap aggregator incident is recorded.

Loss is the approvers' gross depletion: the anchor and 0x077ea419 priced by loss.mjs ($10,002.21), plus the bundle's 599.999 USDC and 1,287.86 USDT at par ($1,887.74 with USDC at 0.9998). The wallets' approvals to the aggregator, not to its transfer proxy as swapIn expects, are user state; the defect is the unrestricted call.
